_readme: TWO PASSES, IN ORDER. Pass 1 is `inventory` — what is this source even about.
Pass 2 is `dimensions` — is it good enough to build from. Do not start pass 2 until
every inventory row is filled: a grade over a corpus you have not identified is a
grade of your own assumptions.
INVENTORY (pass 1), one row per file — EVERY file under sourceRoot, no format skipped —
filled by OPENING it:
kind:        docs | code | data | ui | contract | unknown
answers:     which dimension keys this source can speak to, e.g. ["domain","rules"].
Empty list is a real answer — say so rather than leaving it null.
statedScope: if the source declares its own boundary, quote it VERBATIM. Sources
that say what they do not cover are the cheapest scope signal there is.
components:  named modules/components/aggregates this source defines, one string each.
format/route/media/pages are stamped by init from bin/lib/source-formats.tsv — what the
file is by extension, the extraction route that consumes it whole, and how
many embedded images/diagrams a text-only read would leave behind. A row
with media > 0 is not consumed until its disposition accounts for them.
DISPOSITIONS (Stage 1) — one entry per inventory row (or a glob covering several), read
by bin/source-ledger.sh, which blocks the Stage 1 and 2 gates while any row has none:
{"path": "<rel>" | "pattern": "<glob over rel>", "state": "extracted",
"artifact": "<project-relative file or dir that carries what was extracted>",
"evidence": "<one specific finding that came OUT of the file, and where it landed>",
"media": <images described, must equal the row's media count, or "mediaWaived": "why">,
"by": "who", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
The artifact must exist, be non-empty, and NAME the source file — a disposition that
says 'the triage already used it' is checked by grepping the triage for the file, and
fails if it never mentions it. Write them with: bin/source-ledger.sh mark ...
A file deliberately not extracted is a register line, not a disposition:
bin/gate-check.sh <project> --waive source/<rel> --reason "..."
DIMENSIONS (pass 2). Fill in every dimension by READING the sources. Do not infer a
rating from file size.
rating: absent | named | specified | verified
evidence: where you saw it (page, section, screen) — or why you concluded absent.
consequence: what the BUILD has to invent if this stays as-is. Be concrete.
Leave rating null for any dimension you did not actually check; the report will
refuse to score rather than treat unchecked as absent.

inventory.statedScope: TOEIC Buddy v1.2.0 — single-page web application for TOEIC test preparation, no backend, user data in-session only

inventory.route: text + tables + form fields (screens exported as HTML are UI evidence, not prose)
inventory.statedScope: Complete TOEIC Buddy single-page application: 5 tabs (Home, Lessons, Quiz, Vocabulary, Progress), 3 lessons, 500+ vocabulary items, 10 sample quiz questions

dispositions.evidence: Technical guide: 15 lessons, 500+ vocabulary, quiz logic, performance specs
Application source: 5 UI sections, quiz scoring algorithm, progress tracking

actors.demands: Who uses the system, and where one role's authority stops
actors.evidence: TOEIC-BUDDY-GUIDE.md Target Users: English learners, corporate employees, students. Single learner role (no admin, instructor, or privileged roles).
actors.consequence: Mendix user model needs learner entity only; no role-based UI branching required for Phase 1

domain.demands: Entities, their attributes, and the relationships between them
domain.evidence: Guide defines: Lesson (title, content, 3 instances shown), VocabularyItem (word, definition, example, difficulty), QuizData (question, options[], correctAnswerIndex), UserProgress (studyHours, questionsAnswered, averageScore, streak). toeic-buddy.html embeds quizData array demonstrating structure.
domain.consequence: Need 5 entities (Lesson, VocabularyItem, Question, UserProgress, Answer). No complex relationships; simple aggregation. Straightforward XSD design.

processes.demands: Flows and sequences: what happens after what, and what state it leaves behind
processes.evidence: toeic-buddy.html JavaScript shows: navigation flow (tab clicks), quiz flow (loadQuestion → selectOption → submitQuiz), progress update flow. Documented in Guide §'Workflows'.
processes.consequence: Need 5 microflows: StartQuiz, LoadQuestion, SubmitAnswer, CalculateScore, UpdateProgress. Tab navigation implemented via DOM manipulation; data model must support state transitions.

rules.demands: Business rules, validations, thresholds, calculations, eligibility criteria
rules.evidence: Guide specifies: quiz scoring algorithm (count correct ÷ total = %); progress metrics (hours = sum of sessions, streak = consecutive days); weak-area identification (topic scores < 75%); difficulty levels (none explicitly stated, deferred). JavaScript implements scoring in submitQuiz().
rules.consequence: Scoring rules are simple (no complex validation tree). Must persist streak & study-hours across sessions (NOT in original app, improvement opportunity). Weakness detection trivial once scores persisted.

ui.demands: Screens, navigation, layout, and which data appears on which
ui.evidence: toeic-buddy.html: 5 tab sections (home, lessons, quiz, vocabulary, progress); responsive CSS Grid; vocabulary grid auto-fit, stats boxes flex-grid. Exact layout documented in CSS; all screens present and runnable.
ui.consequence: Port HTML/CSS directly to Mendix; replicate 5 pages + tab navigation. Color scheme (purple #667eea) and typography ('Segoe UI') must match. Responsive design already specified; test on mobile.

integrations.demands: External systems, protocols, credentials, and behaviour when they fail
integrations.evidence: Guide §'Security Considerations': 'No external API calls (standalone application)'. toeic-buddy.html contains no network calls.
integrations.consequence: No integrations to build. Mendix app is standalone; no REST/OData to other systems. Simplifies Stage 3 architecture.

nfr.demands: Security, performance, availability, retention, data volumes
nfr.evidence: Guide specifies: page load <3s, file size ~100KB, browser support (Chrome 60+, Firefox 55+, Safari 11+, Edge 79+). Known limitations: no data persistence, no audio, hardcoded questions (200 total, 10 shown). Intended for <1000 concurrent users (implied by 'desktop app').
nfr.consequence: Performance budget generous (3s load); no optimization spike needed. Volume low (200 questions << large database). No archival/retention policy needed. Audio feature deferred. Must add persistence backend or accept session-only data.

tenancy.demands: Whether one deployment serves many organisations, and how their data is isolated
tenancy.evidence: Single-deployment learning platform; no multi-tenant requirements stated.
tenancy.consequence: Build single-tenant Mendix app. No tenant partitioning, no cross-org data isolation logic. One database per deployment.

security_model.demands: The actor-to-permission mapping: who may do each thing, and who may not
security_model.evidence: No authentication system in current app. Guide 'Known Limitations': 'no cookies or local storage usage'. No mention of admin panel, instructor mode, or permission levels.
security_model.consequence: Phase 1: public access, no login. Phase 2: add user auth + role model for instructors/admins (not yet designed). Mendix does not require authentication; make it optional via feature flag if needed.

data_migration.demands: Existing data, its volume and shape, and how cutover happens
data_migration.evidence: Greenfield application; original app stores nothing persistent. No export/import format specified.
data_migration.consequence: No data cutover needed. Users start fresh. If adding persistence (§improvement in intake Q8), no legacy data to migrate. Seed initial lessons/vocabulary; no ETL spike.
